I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks cleanly. `tsc` only reports errors in `src/module.ts`, because lodash isn't installed in this project.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 2364 bytes (min+gzip) and 97 bytes of own code. I couldn't measure the original's size, since lodash isn't installed and the original can't be bundled. I didn't run the full set of grading inputs through the migrated file. I only compared a few hand-picked inputs, listed below.

The installed es-toolkit is 1.53.2. The imports and their sources are:

| Function | Import | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `merge` | `es-toolkit` (main) | It gave the same results as the compat version on my test patches, which covered nested objects, arrays merged by index, and null overwritten by a number. The main `merge` is also smaller: the compat one took the bundle from 2364 to 4044 bytes. It mutates `base` and returns it, like lodash. |
| `startCase` | `es-toolkit/compat` | The main `startCase` differs from lodash on consecutive capitals: `XMLHttp2Go` becomes `Xml Http 2 Go`, where lodash and compat give `XML Http 2 Go`. Your input range includes consecutive capitals, so main would fail the equality check. |
| `truncate` | `es-toolkit/compat` | The main package has no `truncate`. The compat one gave `xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx...` for a 30-character string with `{ length: 24 }`, which I believe matches lodash. I didn't compare it against lodash directly. |

No lodash import remains, and nothing is hand-written beyond the three original wrapper functions.
